text.p: Playing under the lights Thursday night worked against Czech top seed Jana Novotna at the Bausch & Lomb Championships as she fell to 12th-seeded South African Amanda Coetzer 6-2 1-6 6-1.

"I had a problem seeing the ball since I only play under the lights once or twice during the year," the fourth-ranked Novotna said. "I knew she was a tough player and she has a good record against top players. I wasn't going for my first serves and was missing many overheads and easy volleys."
Second seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario and fourth seed Conchita Martinez, both Spaniards, scored third-round victories on a chilly Florida afternoon to move into the quarter-finals.

The fifth-ranked Sanchez Vicario won a 6-3 1-6 6-4 encounter over 16th seed Ruxandra Dragomir of Romania in a long two hours, 35 minutes. Sanchez Vicario now has a 4-0 career edge over Dragomir with all of their meetings coming on clay.
Sanchez Vicario, a former three-time Grand Slam singles champion, has not won a trophy since May 1996 in Hamburg, Germany.
The sixth-ranked Martinez captured a 6-3 6-3 victory over 30th-ranked American Chanda Rubin in a brief 65 minutes. Martinez has beaten Rubin all five times they have played.

Friday's quarter-final pairings pit Coetzer against ninth seed Mary Joe Fernandez of the United States, Sanchez Vicario against 11th seed Mary Pierce of France, Martinez against eighth seed Iva Majoli of Croatia, and sixth seed Lindsay Davenport of the United States against Jana Kandarr of Germany.

The 14th-ranked Coetzer did not have problems with the lights during the one hour, 24 minute match. She had tested the evening playing conditions Wednesday night in an exhibition match with Davenport after Jennifer Capriati withdrew with a sprained leg muscle.

"I really enjoyed it out there," said Coetzer, who is now 2-2 in head-to-head meetings with Novotna. "I started off really well, which gave me a nice boost. I felt good right from the start. I played a solid match."

After taking the first set with relative ease, Coetzer faced a more aggressive Novotna in the second set. The South African held serve in the first game of the second set but dropped the next six games and the set.

Coetzer started the third set strongly, breaking Novotna's serve in the first game. Novotna held serve once in the final set, in the third game. The South African won the match on her third match point when Novotna, serving, blasted a forehand way out of bounds.

Finishing the match was a monumental challenge for the 21st-ranked Dragomir, who started cramping in the eighth game of the final set. The cramping started in her right calf, then was in both calves, and by the end of the match was moving up into her thighs.
Despite her discomfort, Dragomir evened the score to 4-4 before allowing Sanchez Vicario to close out the match by winning the final two games.

"When you have cramps you're better off moving than staying (in one place) because your muscle gets so tight if you don't move," Dragomir said. "It was like having two opponents -- fighting her and fighting cramps."

Sanchez Vicario, who faced three break points on her serve in the ninth game of the third set, found it difficult to pay attention to the match with Dragomir so obviously in pain on the other side of the net.

"I was watching her more then trying to play my game," Sanchez Vicario admitted. "Anybody that has that situation is looking at the opponent to see their reaction. Definitely she was in pain, but she was able to run, so I did try to move her around."
Sanchez Vicario, played a good first set, but fell apart in the second set. She only held her serve in the sixth game and won a total of six points in three service games.
"I lost my concentration in the second set," Sanchez Vicario said.
There were eight service breaks in the two-set match between the sixth-ranked Martinez and Rubin.
Martinez, who surprised the tennis world by winning Wimbledon in 1994, is glad to be back on the clay courts.
"It's a lot of fun to go out there and slide on clay," Martinez said. "And to go for every ball. In the second set, I just played well and didn't give her any chance to come back."
